input: Gandantegchinlen Monastery / Гандантэгчинлэн хийд, Улаанбаатар, Монгол / BGD - 16 khoroo, Ulaanbaatar 16040, Mongolia
note: One input carrying the SAME address twice — a Cyrillic/Mongolian rendering and a Latin/English one, slash-joined — so venue, locality and country each have two correct surface forms present at once ('Улаанбаатар' and 'Ulaanbaatar'; 'Монгол' and 'Mongolia'). This row freezes the LATIN half, and that choice exposes a GRADER limit as well as a schema one: a fully correct dual-script parse emits two spans per tag, the harness joins repeats with a space, and the comparison then reads venue = 'Gandantegchinlen Monastery Гандантэгчинлэн хийд' and fails. The better parse scores worse. Recorded here rather than worked around, because the fix belongs in the check, not in the truth. BGD = Баянгол дүүрэг, taken as attested by the oracle rather than independently adjudicated. Oracle: https://maps.app.goo.gl/r7XN3J1acXYJxsp5A -> 'Gandantegchinlen Monastery' @ !3d47.9231136 !4d106.8949841. 2026-08-11: the grader repair this note asked for landed as the per-row expectComponentRenderings contract — venue, locality and country now require BOTH attested renderings (each sourced verbatim from this input); expectComponents keeps the frozen Latin halves, superseded per key by the contract.

Ulaanbaatar addresses by düüreg (district) then khoroo (sub-district), and the input abbreviates the first in Cyrillic: ХУД = Хан-Уул дүүрэг, Khan-Uul District. THREE scripts are in play across two fields — Cyrillic abbreviation, Cyrillic common noun (хороо), Latin city and country — and the oracle adds a fourth rendering by transliterating the abbreviation: https://maps.app.goo.gl/GFYRfxiyHftWUGiW8 canonicalizes to 'HUD - 15 khoroo, Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia' @ !3d47.9044014 !4d106.9183885. The district and the khoroo are two NESTED admin levels and the union carries one `dependent_locality`, so both are folded into a single span here. The `district` tag is not reused for the düüreg on purpose: it is declared JP-specific (大字) and belongs to the JP char model's head vocabulary, so borrowing it for Mongolian would overload a locale-scoped tag across two unrelated address systems. SCHEMA GAP: district/khoroo as separate sub-locality levels.

input: National University of Mongolia, WWF9+6H6, SBD - 6 khoroo, Ulaanbaatar 14200, Mongolia
note: 'WWF9+6H6' is an Open Location Code (plus code) in local short form — a base-20 encoding of a coordinate cell, resolved against the city named later in the same string. It is NOT a postcode, and this row is the sharp version of that claim because a REAL postcode, 14200, sits four tokens away: a model that types the plus code as `postcode` emits two postcode spans and the harness joins them, so the error is visible in the value rather than hidden in a coin flip. The union has no coordinate-encoding tag. SCHEMA GAP: plus code / Open Location Code.
